overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by untimely approving minutes for five 2023 meetings, and declined to review the records-request, broad minutes, and notice-specificity allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to provide certification forms and meeting minutes in response to a June 22 public records request.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this first allegation concerns the Board’s compliance with the Public Records Law, G.L. c. 66, § 10, not the Open Meeting Law, and we therefore decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely create and approve minutes for meetings held in 2022 and 2023.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether the minutes from 2022 and the minutes for the Board’s March 9, 2023, meeting were timely approved where the July 20 complaint was filed more than 30 days after the latest set of minutes was approved in open session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve open session minutes for March 23, April 13, May 4, May 11, and May 25, 2023 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board failed to timely approve minutes for meetings held on March 23, April 13, May 4, May 11, and May 25, 2023, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged notices for all 2023 Board meetings were vague and misleading, specifically those for June 8 and June 22.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons as discussed above, we decline to review the July 24 complaint where we do not conduct broad audits of public bodies and where the complaint is untimely with respect to the two meetings specifically identified.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of the date of the letter, approve any of the identified meeting minutes that have not yet been approved.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Board, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to approve any of the above meeting minutes which have not yet been approved.
